name: Judd Foundation
funding: FY2025-26 supporters include Bloomberg Philanthropies, Texas Commission on the Arts, Henry Moore Foundation, Japan Foundation, Villa Albertine, Neuberger Berman, Gagosian and Bristol Myers Squibb, plus many patrons and individuals.
watch: Maintains Donald Judd's permanently installed living and working spaces in Marfa and 101 Spring Street, New York.
why_flagged: Bloomberg Philanthropies is campaigned against elsewhere, not at Judd. Contributions were $966K of $12.6M revenue in FY2025.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990 filings are on ProPublica, a named supporters list is published each year to FY2025, and the board is listed.

name: Kaesong Koryo Museum
watch: Hall 3 is usually closed to foreigners. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State-run museum in Kaesong with over 1,000 Koryo-dynasty artefacts in four halls and an open-air stone collection; 20,000 m², 12 main buildings.
records_note: A North Korean state museum; searches found no website, report, accounts, donor list or board.

name: Karachi Biennale Trust
funding: Philanthropists and corporate sponsors, not itemised.
watch: Name to know: K-Electric, Karachi's mostly thermal power utility. Engro (Thar coal) was KB22 lead partner. 2019 censorship row.
why_flagged: Name to know: K-Electric, Karachi's mostly thermal power utility. Engro (Thar coal) was KB22 lead partner. 2019 censorship row.
records_note: It posts a trustee list of ten names and sponsor logos by edition (KB24 partners), but no annual report and no accounts.

name: Kemper Museum
watch: 2019 artist protests over a trustee tied to ICE detention litigation.
why_flagged: 2019 artist protests over a trustee tied to ICE detention litigation.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2021 to 2024 with named honor rolls and trustees, and its Form 990 is public through 2024.

name: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra)
why_flagged: Established, built and run by Saudi Aramco, the national oil company, 82% owned by the Saudi government.
records_note: Ithra posts 2023 and 2024 annual reports; its parent Aramco posts reports for 2019 to 2025 with financials and an 11-member board.

name: Kiran Nadar Museum of Art
watch: In July 2023 it fired Sandip K Luis over a post criticising Nadar's role in a state exhibition. Shahidul Alam pulled his show.
why_flagged: Private museum founded and chaired by collector Kiran Nadar, free to visit. Its home page names no funders.
records_note: KNMA posts FCRA financial statements for 2014-15 to 2024-25 and lists its trustees and advisers, but no annual report or donor list.

name: Kochi-Muziris Biennale
watch: In December 2022, 47 artists and six collectives published an open letter citing poor communication and opaque finances. Founder Bose Krishnamachari resigned in January 2026.
why_flagged: Funded by Kerala state grants and private donors. Its 2025-26 site names no sponsors; a December 2025 headline records philanthropist Minal Bajaj's support.
records_note: Kochi-Muziris Biennale names benefactors, patrons and supporters for its 2025 edition and lists ten trustees, but posts no annual report or accounts.

name: Koorie Heritage Trust
watch: Viva Energy, an oil refiner and fuel retailer, is a fossil-fuel funder. It became Principal Corporate Supporter in December 2018 (Viva press release). The 2022-23 annual report still names it a key sponsor: it funds the Oral History program and the Viva Energy Australia 3D Award at the Koorie Art Show. No newer annual report has been published and no protest was found. Other names: Lendlease (property), ANZ (bank), RMIT.
why_flagged: Viva Energy, an oil refiner and fuel retailer, is a fossil-fuel funder. It became Principal Corporate Supporter in December 2018 (Viva press release). The 2022-23 annual report still names it a key sponsor: it funds the Oral History program and the Viva Energy Australia 3D Award at the Koorie Art Show. No newer annual report has been published and no protest was found. Other names: Lendlease (property), ANZ (bank), RMIT.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2008 to 2023 with full financial statements, a partners and sponsors section and the board.

name: Korean Art Gallery
funding: Workers' Party of Korea state budget.
watch: The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: National fine-art museum with 22 display rooms; KCNA claimed 6 million cumulative visitors by 2020. Budget unpublished.
records_note: Its listed address, korart.sca.kp, does not resolve from outside North Korea, so no records could be checked.

name: Korean Central History Museum
watch: Kim Jong Un's 2014 speech called it a model for history museums. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: About 100,000 relics in 19 halls over 10,500 m². The museum claimed 10 million cumulative visitors by 2015; Kim Il Sung founded it in 1945.
records_note: A North Korean state museum; no official website, report, accounts, donor list or board turned up.

name: Kuindzhi Art Museum
funding: A Ukrainian city museum until 2022. Under Russian occupation it is run by the culture ministry of the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, which the US, EU and UK list as a sanctioned entity.
watch: Its Kuindzhi paintings were taken to a museum in Donetsk after the city fell in 2022.
why_flagged: A Ukrainian city museum until 2022. Under Russian occupation it is run by the culture ministry of the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, which the US, EU and UK list as a sanctioned entity.
records_note: The museum was destroyed in March 2022 and no official site, report, accounts, funder list or board turned up.

name: Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg
watch: Det Obelske Familiefond holds about 14.5% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
why_flagged: Det Obelske Familiefond holds about 14.5% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
records_note: Kunsten posts annual reports from 2016 to 2025 with accounts, names its funding foundations in the 2021 report, and lists its six-person board.
